title: After six weeks off, the Target tells a member to start lighter and also to push to one rep from failure
what: The plan week is counted by the calendar from the day the plan was followed, with no regard for weeks the member did not train. A member who logs how hard sets felt and comes back after 6 or more weeks away gets a Target that says "8 weeks since your last Squat. Start lighter and build back." and, in the same note, "This week of your plan, stop each set with about 1 rep left in the tank (RPE 9)" whenever the calendar lands on the end of a block. The first week back can also be the planned easy week, and the plan line reads "Week 15" for a member who trained 5 weeks of it.
expected: A long break pauses the plan week count, or at least the effort line is left off a Target that is already a lighter comeback, so the two halves of one note never pull opposite ways.
who: members following a plan who log effort
how_often: after any break of 6 weeks or more, on about 2 weeks in 5
fix_line: Leave the effort sentence off a comeback Target, and let a long break hold the plan week count

title: The Statistics sets headline is much lower than its own bars added up
what: On Statistics the line over the sets chart reads like "412 sets since 7 Sep" and is described as the total of every bar. But the headline counts each set once, while each bar counts a set once for every body group it touches. With all six groups picked (the default), one bench press set is 1 set in the headline and 2 in the bars (chest, shoulders, arms). A member who taps the bars and adds them up gets a number far above the headline, with nothing on screen saying why.
expected: The headline and the bars are counted the same way, or the screen says the headline counts each set once while the bars count it for every group.
how_often: every time, unless one group is picked
fix_line: Count the bars and the headline by the same rule, or add a short line saying how they differ

title: The monthly report compares a new member's first full month with the few days they trained the month before
what: A member whose first workout was on 25 October opens the November report and reads "You trained 14 times in November - 12 more than October", with green "+12" and "+500%" tiles. October only held their first week. The Statistics screen already refuses this comparison ("Your log is too new to compare") for exactly this case, but the monthly report has no such check.
expected: The 'Against last month' tiles and the coach sentence only compare with a month the member's log fully covers, as Statistics does.
how_often: once, in each new member's second month report
fix_line: Skip the month-before comparison when the first workout falls inside that month

title: A month with a planned easy week shows red drops in sets and kg lifted with no reason given
what: An easy week halves the sets on purpose. The monthly report counts those workouts like any other, so a month that held one shows a red drop in sets and kg lifted against the month before, and the coach note says nothing about the easy week. The Progress page already treats an easy week as "not a dip", so the two places tell the member different stories about the same weeks.
expected: When the month held an easy week, the report says so beside the drop (or leaves those workouts out of the comparison), as Progress does.
who: members following a plan with easy weeks on
fix_line: Mark easy-week workouts in the report and name the easy week when the month dropped

title: Profile and Statistics give different workout counts for "the last 3 months"
what: The Profile chart says "Kg lifted in the last 3 months - 27 workouts" but it counts whole weeks back to the Monday before 90 days ago, so it covers 91 to 97 days. The Statistics screen's "Last 3 months" tiles count exactly 91 days. A member who trained in those few extra days sees two different numbers under the same words.
expected: "The last 3 months" covers the same days on both screens, or Profile names the date it counts from.
how_often: most weeks, when a workout falls in the extra days
fix_line: Use one span for "last 3 months", or say "since <date>" under the Profile total

items.reason: Gym facts (alerts, dues, plan end, birthdays) do not live here; this area works out the member's own training numbers kept on the phone, so Crispy Curves rows hold none of them. Compared by code: workouts in the last 3 months (Profile vs Statistics), month against month (report vs Statistics), weeks in a row (badge vs streak rule: same rule, longest vs current by design).
